description.narrative: The development objectives of the Multi-Sectoral Technical Assistance Project for Mongolia are to support the recipient's efforts to enhance its capacity for policy making, regulation, and implementation in the fiscal, social, and financial sectors. The project will provide four components as follows: (a) enhancing capacity for fiscal management in the ministry of finance to better implement a budget that is fiscally sustainable and better linked to national. local, and sectoral priorities; (b) strengthening the capacity of the ministry of social welfare and labor to improve the efficacy of social expenditure by designing and implementing a targeted poverty benefit; (c) enhancing capacity of the Bank of Mongolia for maintaining financial sector stability by intensifying supervision and implementing a bank restructuring strategy; and (d) the existing project management unit responsible for both the Governance Assistance Project and Economic Capacity Technical Assistance (TA) Project will also provide its services for this TA Project.
To support the Recipient's efforts to enhance its capacity for policy making, regulation, and implementation in the fiscal, social,and financial sectors.

title.narrative: Improve the templates used for financial reporting in accordance with IFRS and create a consolidated database system for allowing electronic filing of financial statements by firms

baseline.value: Existing template ineffective due to modifications to IFRS. Lack of capacity and inefficiency of the current software - eBalance

target.value: IFRS-complied accounting guidelines for entities along with the revised chart of accounts obtained approval by the Minister of Finance on December 23, 2014 (order #249). The e-balance system for electronic submission of financial statements was upgraded and implemented 2013 Q1. Data conversion for years 2002-2012 was done in December 2014. The upgraded e-balance system is now fully operational with access to past years data to perform analytics. All entities above a certain size operating in Mongolia are now submitting their financial statements through the online e-balance system of the MOF

actual.value: Regular financial statement e-filing to the MOF through the e-balance system

title.narrative: Capacity enhancement for setting and enforcing international financial reporting standards (IFRS)

baseline.value: Lack of capacity for both regulators and preparers of financial statements with regards to IFRS.

target.value: Efforts to build capacity of the financial statement preparers, Accounting and Auditing Standards Committee members and other regulators continue under the project through provision of IFRS and IFRS for SME training. So far approximately 2750 accounting professionals nationwide have been trained during 100+ training events organized in 2012-2016. Preparation of guidance notes and regulations as well as the improved e-balance system have been also contributing to enhanced capacity.

title.narrative: Transparency on procurement process managed by the GPA will be enhanced according to the revised Public Procurement Law

baseline.value: Limited disclosure of information on contract awardees, and contract cost.

target.value: Achieved. information on all the bidders that participated in tenders organized by the GPA have been disclosed on the Government website and all tender procedures have been conducted online. In addition, results of all announced bid and contract awardees managed by the GPA are 100 percent disclosed to the public.

title.narrative: MPDSP has prepared a poor households database, on the basis of the Proxy Means Test survey.

target.value: The second round of PMT survey data collection was completed in December 2013, and the database became available in April 2014.

comment.narrative: Achieved. The database contained rich and comprehensive data for 712,440 households and 2,880,742 individuals, which covered 89.2 percent of total households in Mongolia. The scores of 662,514 households were calculated and ranked.

title.narrative: Fiscal transfer formula for local government financing improved to increase predictability of resources and to reduce horizontal inequities between local governments and facilities

target.value: The Methodology for Transferring Revenue from the General Local Development Fund to the Local Development Fund approved by Government resolution #30. The formula for LDF allocation was changed in order to reduce inequality of the fund per person allocated from the General Local Development Fund. In addition, the revised version of financing methodology for primary health care services provided by soums and villages was approved by joint order #498/345 in December 2015 of the Minister of Finance and Ministry of Health and Sport. Variable cost standard normative on preschool and secondary education was approved by Government resolution #242 in 2016, which included average variable cost normative per student at various levels of education.

comment.narrative: Achieved. This revision was to reflect various forms of government regulations beyond government resolutions and also to give more flexibility considering varying progress in improving financing mechanisms of different spending objectives.

actual.value: Government regulations are adopted and implemented to improve the financing mechanisms to local governments

title.narrative: MoPDSP and GOSWS have created an adequate IT infrastructure for designated users on the basis of the PMT database for poor households and citizens or targeting purposes for social programs, assist

target.value: The database was initially used for only one welfare program—the Food Stamp Program. The regulation for ISDB authorized users/ usage and maintenance of integrated household information database is developed and approved by Government Decree # 404 dated 30 Dec, 2014. Since then, the database was used for targeting of the Child Money Program starting from 2016 and was later used for targeted medical health insurance, free textbooks for children from poor households, and free legal advocacy services for the poor. The ISDB iscurrently functioning 8 approved authorized users.

title.narrative: Strengthened legal framework for prudent natural resource revenue management.

baseline.value: No legal framework for prudent natural resource revenue management exited.

target.value: The new law on Mongolia's natural resource fund (Future Heritage Fund Law) was adopted in December 2015. With support from the consultants hired under the project, the MOF initiated work to set up a road map comprising preparatory work necessary to set up a well-functioning long-term savings fund, which is expected to begin accumulation of mineral revenues in 3–4 years.

title.narrative: Strengthened fiscal planning and management capacity through improving budget planning mechanism

baseline.value: No on-line web-based Budget Planning Information System existed for budget preparation and different char of accounts are used for budget planning (Fiscal, budget planning system) and execution (GFMIS) systems

target.value: The web-based Budget Preparation and Information System (BPIS) has been introduced under the project to prepare budget proposals and allocate expenditures. The system has become functional for the local budget planning process cycle for 2016 and 2017 budgets. However, the BPIS only became operational for budget planning at the local level, but not yet at the central level.

comment.narrative: Partially achieved. The revision of original target is to further include the local government as the users of the BPIS system. Adopting the BPIS nationwide has been a key component under the follow-up Strengthening Fiscal and Financial Stability (SFFS) Project, which is expected to be fully achieved by 2022.

title.narrative: State Bank is restructured and its privatization announced.

baseline.value: State Bank is owned by the Government. No privatization plan is established.

target.value: The privatization plan of State Bank was announced, but only partially restructured. A Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) was signedby the BOM, MOF, and State Bank in May 2017 on detailed actions with a goal to complete the privatization by January 2019. Coordinating processes of the above three legal bodies reflected in the MOU are in progress. Politically, however, the momentum for reform has waned with the recovery of the State Bank's financial performance. Privatization is not expected in the foreseeable future. Nevertheless, internal restructuring is going on as part of the restructuring strategy. Deloitte conducted independent audits to evaluatethe State Bank's financial statements. Financial standards and corporate governance of the State Bank have improved throughout the reform progress.

title.narrative: Percentage of staff trained in the Ministry of Population Development and Social Protection, General Office for Social Welfare Service and local governments

baseline.value: unknown due to govt restructuring in 2012

target.value: Out of a total number of 1,538 staffs nationwide, 1,311 social welfare staffs were trained through 161 local trainings, overseas study tours, and workshops and 885 staffs received certificates on passing the final training test on how to use the WAIS software.

baseline.value: Institutional framework for risk-based macro-prudential regulation and supervision is not established.

target.value: A medium-term banking supervision strategy incorporating a detailed plan for transition to Basel II and III standards was developedand is being implemented at the BOM. To adopt forward-looking and risk-based supervision, a macro-stress testing framework was developed and is being used in risk assessment. However, some of the documents developed under the project, including the draft regulation on enforcement and prompt corrective measure for banks, regulation on risk-based supervision and its manual, and the IT inspection manual, were neither applied nor approved.

title.narrative: The Government shall have submitted to the Parliament for passing the draft laws on accounting and auditing that would create the legal environment for ensuring that Mongolia's accounting and auditing

target.value: Draft laws submitted to the Parliament and approved by Parliament in its plenary session held on June 18, 2015. The revised laws become effective January 1, 2016.

title.narrative: New deposit insurance agency is fully operational.

baseline.value: New Law on Deposit Insurance Corporation enacted and is about to have its implementation started

target.value: The Mongolia Deposit Insurance Corporation (DICOM) was established in 2013 and has received MNT 250 billion of capital injection. The new agency is already equipped with a functioning information system and internal procedures on risk pay-out compensation in linewith international standards.

comment.narrative: Almost achieved. The new deposit insurance agency is almost fully operational. However, there are further tasks to achieve the goal that the new Deposit Insurance Corporation becomes a full-fledged pillar of the financial sector safety net, with proper institutioal structure and financial capacity, deposit payout capacities, and clear mandates and responsibilities, as suggested by a Core Principles Assessment of the DICOM conducted in December 2016.Continued support by the SFFS Project and the World Bank's Financial Sector Development Support Program would remain an important vehicle in further strengthening the DICOM's capacity.

title.narrative: A strategy paper, policy options and main concept driving the pension reform agenda have been submitted to the Government , and animplementation plan has been developed

baseline.value: Despite the govt intention to move to a multitier pension system, the actual strategy has not been defined yet.

target.value: Pension reform policy options were developed that aimed to establish a multi-pillar pension system that would provide adequate retirement benefits to the Mongolian elderly. These policy options were considered when the government developing its State Pension Reform Policy for 2015–2030, which was officially approved by Parliament decree #53 dated on June 11, 2015.

baseline.value: No IFRS in place for financial sector

target.value: IFRS for banks has been introduced and the banks requested to comply with the new accounting standards starting January 2016. For successful implementation of approved accounting standards, a new online reporting system, Financial Information and National Accounting system (FINA), which enables supervisors to promptly extract reports and information from database and make consolidated financial statements of banking sector and individual banks, was installed and the commercial banks have started submitting their financialreports through the system from July 1, 2016.

title.narrative: By the Closing Date, the Recipient shall have reduced its structural deficit according to the deficit ceilings set forth in the Fiscal Stability Law.

baseline.value: In 2014, the general government budget recorded a deficit equivalent to 4% of GDP, above the FSL's deficit ceiling of 2% of GDP.

target.value: In 2016, the structural budget deficit in Mongolia stood at 15.3 percent of GDP, which was within the deficit ceiling of the FSL. Nevertheless, budget deficit increased sharply in 2016 due to a revenue decline amid a commodity price drop, and an unexpected increase in expenditures because of the June General Election in 2016. However, the budget deficit was significantly reduced to 6.3 percent of GDP in 2017, successfully achieving the annual structural budget deficit target of 10.4 percent of GDP according to the revisedFSL.

comment.narrative: This PDO indicator was achieved for the calendar year 2017. The reference date for the target for this indicator is June 30, 2017. However, the structural deficit ceiling set forth in the FSL is on an annual basis and therefore it was not possible to calculate mid-year when the project closed in June 2017. Hence, the reference date of December 30, 2017 is adopted for the assessment of the achievement. Overall, the effects to ensure stability and countercyclical fiscal policy in line with the sub-objective of the MSTA project once went off track. However, strong corrective actions have been taken since late 2016. The institutional progress made under this MSTA project remained highly relevant under the current reform programs that seeks to put Mongolia back and more firmly on track for responsible and countercyclical fiscal policy.
